guidance: In a normative requirement, MUST, REQUIRED, and SHALL express obligation; translate as “必须”. Preserve the actor and scope.
SHOULD and RECOMMENDED express strong recommendations that can have justified exceptions; use “应当/建议”, not an unconditional MUST. SHOULD NOT or NOT RECOMMENDED means “通常不应/不建议”, not an absolute ban.
MAY or OPTIONAL expresses permission/optionality (“可以/可选”). In “may be” expressing uncertainty, translate possibility (“可能”), not permission.
MUST NOT, SHALL NOT, and prohibited express a prohibition (“不得/禁止”). Keep the prohibition attached to the correct actor and operation.

UNLESS introduces an exception/condition, usually “除非”; EXCEPT WHEN is “除……情况外”. PROVIDED THAT introduces a condition (“前提是/仅当”). Preserve whether the base rule applies inside or outside the exception.
ONLY IF states a necessary condition, not a sufficient one (“仅当/只有……才”). IF AND ONLY IF is biconditional (“当且仅当”). Preserve both/all vs at-least-one scope.
Preserve inclusivity and units: at least/no fewer than ≥ (“至少”), at most/no more than ≤ (“至多/不超过”), more than > (“超过”), less than < (“少于”). Keep numeric values and units unchanged.

Preserve event order and endpoint inclusivity. BEFORE/AFTER are relative to the named event; UNTIL is “直至/直到”; within X is “在 X 之内”; no later/earlier than is inclusive unless the text states otherwise.
Keep each requirement attached to the named protocol role. A client, server, proxy, cache, and implementation are distinct actors; do not broaden a role-specific rule.
Preserve security/privacy boundaries and authorization conditions. Do not turn an optional application choice into automatic behavior or remove a prohibition on retaining or resending data.
Distinguish generation from parsing and a grammar rule from an implementation choice. Preserve whether a parser must accept input or a generator must emit it.
Preserve the direction and scope of cross-references, precedence, and registry actions; update/replace does not mean merely cite or copy.
